_: Hearing loss must exceed specified decibel criteria, $1,510 annual limit for aids and supplies applicable to nonpregnant and noninstitutionalized adults, can be exceeded for authorization.
One hearing aid in each ear every 3 years and one cochlear implant in each ear with internal replacement as medically necessary.

Bone Anchored Hearing Aids. For recipients who have documented profound, severe hearing loss in one or both ears as follows: Implanted device for recipients age five years and older; Non Implantation (softband) device for recipients under the age of five years Cochlear Implant…
House Bill 3503 requires “coverage for hearing instruments and related services for all individuals 65 years of age and older when a hearing care professional prescribes a hearing instrument.”
Coverage up to $3000 per ear every 48 months.
$2,500 per hearing aid, per ear, once every 36 months
Children 15 and under are covered. Coverage for $1,000 per aid, once every 2 years
$1000 per hearing aid per ear every 3 years
up to $2,000 per hearing aid every 36 months.
Coverage limited to newborns only. Coverage amount varies per need of newborn. Newborns covered for screening, audiological assessment and hearing aid purchases
1 hearing aid per ear every 5 years, no limit on cost but deductibles and co-pays may apply
None, covers the cost of one hearing aid per ear (once every 3 years), cochlear implants, and related therapy
1 hearing aid per ear, every 36 months, no limit on cost and no additional deductible or similar restriction

None for hearing aid cost, once every 48 months

$1,000 total, every 24 months. The state Insurance Department issued a bulletin requiring insurance policies to remove age limits (statute applies to children 12 years of age and under) on hearing aid benefits for policies issued on or after January 1, 2016.
Limited to 6 batteries for monaural/12 for binaural aids; boneanchored hearing aid limited to one every 4 years; One dispensing fee allowed for monaural or binaural services
Maximum age rises to 21 for those still enrolled in high school. $2,200 per ear, once every 36 months
up to $3000 for all covered services every 48 months.
No age restrictions. $1,500 per hearing aid, per ear, once every 60 months
$1,400 per aid, every 36 months. Children 5 and under took effect Jan. 1, 2008, children 6-13 took effect Jan. 1, 2009, children 14-18 took effect Jan. 1, 2010
Increased in 2006 from $400 to $2,000, per hearing aid for those under 19. For all others, increased from $400 to $800, per hearing aid once every three years for both groups
$1,000 per aid, 1 hearing aid per ear every 36 months
1 hearing aid/3 years if original no longer serviceable.
$3 per hearing aid $2 per visit. Prior approval required for services based on policy requirements.
1 hearing aid per ear every 3 years and only for specified degrees of hearing loss; repairs limited to 1 per aid per year; prior authorization required for more frequent requests
Age limit applies to hearing aids and cochlear implants. One hearing aid/5 years
